newsitem.title: USA: Pa. 833 MW Beaver Valley 2 nuke trips during test.
newsitem.headline: Pa. 833 MW Beaver Valley 2 nuke trips during test.

text.p: The 833 megawatt (MW) Beaver Valley 2 nuclear power generating unit was again shut during startup testing from its refueling outage, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Wednesday.
In its daily status report, NRC said the unit, in Shippingport, Pa., was manually tripped while testing repair work linked to the reactor vessel head vent system.
Beaver Valley 2 remained in "hot standby" mode, which means it is still ready for restart. The shutdown did not appear to affect the unit's startup schedule, NRC said.
Duquesne Light Co, which operates the unit, said on Tuesday it planned to have Beaver Valley 2 back on line today, and restore it to full service as early as Thursday.
Duquesne officials could not immediately be reached for comment about the shutdown.
The nearby Beaver Valley 1, rated at 810 MW, was operating at full output, the NRC said.
DQE Inc, Duquesne's parent company, owns 47.5 percent of Beaver Valley 1. The remaining 52.5 percent is owned by Ohio Edison Co.
DQE holds 13.7 percent stake in Beaver Valley 2, Ohio Edison (41.9 percent) and Centerior Energy (44.4 percent).
